item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports separating temporal dynamics from multiple concurrent interests. [MiaSRec (SIGIR 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.00986) explicitly challenges last-item dominance: it constructs item-centered session representations and dynamically selects important intents, reporting stronger gains on longer sessions. [MTMISRec (2025)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0957417425008887) partitions histories using an interaction-gap threshold and models within-session and between-session dependencies; its segmentation is threshold-based rather than learned, and its attribute integration requires checking feature availability. [SS4Rec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.08132) combines time-aware and relation-aware state-space models, with discretization steps controlled by observed time intervals and input content. [TiM4Rec (2024 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.16182) introduces a time-aware structured mask into a Mamba2-style architecture, targeting efficient temporal modeling at low embedding dimensions.\n\nResearch implication, rather than an established result: test a small causal bank of interest states with soft routing from item embeddings and log time gaps, plus a learned boundary/reset gate. Retain a last-item residual and compare against SASRec, last-item-only, one-state recurrence, fixed-window pooling, and fixed-gap segmentation under matched capacity. These sources motivate the components but do not establish improvement on the four specified Amazon categories or pinned HR@10 protocol. To separate recency from positional effects, preserve sequence length and positions while masking item content; separately ablate or shuffle historical gaps while preserving item order. Use only timestamps already observed at each prediction prefix. Select using macro validation HR@10 and inspect routing collapse, state utilization, and sensitivity to history length."}
